column3: It directly joins compounded punishment on the Day of Resurrection with remaining in it, closely clarifying the focus's lasting burden.
Turning away from vain speech only broadly parallels turning away from the Reminder that produces the focus's burden.
The ark's selective carrying concerns preservation rather than a person's enduring liability.
It is the immediately preceding cause: turning from the Reminder results in carrying a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
It specifies that misleaders carry their own complete loads and loads caused by leading others astray on that Day.

Being carried in the ark during the flood is a separate rescue image.

Creatures not carrying their provision concerns divine sustenance, not liability.

Transport by animals and ships is unrelated to eschatological bearing.

The request to inherit the garden of bliss is only a positive final-destination counterpart.

It introduces the revealed Reminder from which turning away, in the immediately following verse, produces the lasting burden.
It continues the focus's Day of Resurrection scene with the trumpet and the gathered criminals.
It contrasts the focus's bearer of wrongdoing with one who acts righteously in faith and therefore fears neither injustice nor deprivation.
It gives a further consequence for turning away from God's Reminder, linking that refusal to a constricted life before resurrection.
It states that the punishment of one who transgresses and does not believe God's signs is more severe and more enduring.
It explicitly depicts deniers carrying their burdens on their backs at the sudden Hour and calls that load evil.
It characterizes the punishment of Hell as an inescapably adhering burden, closely paralleling remaining within the focus's load.
It calls Hell an evil settled residence, directly sharpening the focus's description of its burden as evil.
Disobeying God and His messenger while transgressing limits leads to abiding in the Fire and a humiliating punishment.
It states that opposing God and His messenger leads to the Fire of Hell, abiding therein, and disgrace.
It commands the arrogant to enter Hell's gates abiding therein, providing a close punitive-residence parallel.
It describes the cursed as abiding forever in the Fire with no protector or helper.
It repeats the command to enter Hell's gates abiding therein and calls it the evil dwelling of the arrogant.
It identifies Hell as a place lying in wait for the transgressors, setting up their enduring destination.
It explicitly states that the transgressors will remain in Hell for ages.
It makes dying in disbelief lead to abiding in the Fire, a clear persistence-to-enduring-outcome pattern.
It describes a curse resting on its recipients with no relief, a close image of an unending adverse condition.
It says the people of the Fire will seek to leave it but will not leave, making the focus's remaining there concrete.
It names the Fire as the abode of its gathered inhabitants, abiding therein subject to God's will.
It explicitly identifies those who deny the signs and act arrogantly as companions of the Fire abiding therein.
It assigns abiding in the Fire to associators whose works are nullified, joining culpable action to enduring outcome.
It supplies the preceding identity of the wretched who are in the Fire before the ensuing statement of their abiding there.
It makes the loss of one's scale result in abiding in Hell, adding the reckoning dimension of moral weight.
It assigns the dwelling of arrogant fabricators to Hell, a close counterpart to the focus's evil burden.
It depicts the people of the Fire repeatedly returned to it whenever they seek escape, strongly illustrating confinement.
It describes unending punishment in Hell, where death is neither decreed nor the punishment lightened.
